CEDARVALE RETAIL GROUP — FIRE INCIDENT REPORT
Location: Store #14, Northgate | Report No. FIRE-0033
Incident Date: June 6 | Report Date: June 10
Prepared by: Loss Prevention (Lead: Nora Lindqvist)

INCIDENT SUMMARY
At 3:14 p.m. on June 6, a small fire started in the stockroom of Store #14, ignited by an overloaded power strip powering three space heaters that stockroom staff had plugged in that morning during a heating system outage. The store's sprinkler system activated within 90 seconds of the fire starting, and store manager Rafael Obi confirmed the fire was fully extinguished by the time fire department personnel arrived 6 minutes later. No injuries were reported; one employee was in the stockroom at the time and evacuated immediately upon seeing smoke, well before any sprinkler activation occurred.

DAMAGE ASSESSMENT
Fire and water damage combined are estimated at $3,200, covering damaged shelving, a pallet of seasonal inventory, and stockroom flooring. This estimate was confirmed by the insurance adjuster's visit on June 8. The store's sales floor was unaffected structurally, though it was closed to customers for approximately 4 hours during cleanup and fire department clearance, reopening the same day at 7:30 p.m.

ROOT CAUSE
The root cause is an overloaded power strip exceeding its rated capacity, used to power space heaters as a workaround during a heating system outage that had been reported to Facilities two days earlier but not yet resolved. Store policy prohibits space heaters in stockrooms specifically due to this fire risk, a policy staff acknowledged being aware of but did not follow given how cold the stockroom had become that week.

UNRELATED EVENT AT STORE #22
Separately, on June 8, Store #22 experienced a false fire alarm when a smoke detector in its stockroom was triggered by accumulated dust during a shelving reorganization project. Fire department responded and confirmed no fire; this is an unrelated event, involves no actual fire or damage, and this report addresses only the Store #14 incident on June 6. The two events are noted together here only because both surfaced in the same week's regional Loss Prevention summary and should not be conflated as related in any way.

RESPONSE AND REMEDIATION
1. Store #14's heating system was repaired by Facilities on June 7, removing the underlying reason staff brought in space heaters in the first place.
2. All space heaters found on-site were confiscated and a reminder of the no-space-heater policy was issued to all store managers company-wide on June 9.
3. Power strip audit conducted in Store #14's stockroom; two additional overloaded strips were found and corrected during the same visit.

DISCUSSION OF FACILITY-WIDE RESPONSE
Corporate Facilities proposed an immediate fire-suppression system upgrade across all 40 company stores, estimated at $1.2 million total, to add smoke-activated ventilation in addition to existing sprinklers. Given the cost and the fact that the existing sprinkler system performed exactly as designed in this incident, extinguishing the fire in under 90 seconds with minimal damage, leadership decided not to fund an immediate company-wide rollout. Instead, a pilot upgrade will proceed at the 3 stores Facilities has identified as highest-risk based on building age and prior electrical incidents, with results to be reviewed before considering a wider rollout next year.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Complete power strip audits at all 40 stores within 60 days, prioritizing stores with reported heating or cooling issues in the past year.
2. Track heating/cooling repair tickets for SLA compliance going forward, given the two-day delay contributed directly to this incident.
3. Proceed with the 3-store pilot fire-suppression upgrade; revisit the company-wide rollout decision after 6 months of pilot data.

SIGN-OFF
Approved by Nora Lindqvist, Loss Prevention Lead, June 10.

FRANCHISE AGREEMENT
Between Golden Griddle Quick-Service Franchising LLC ("Franchisor") and Marisol Vega ("Franchisee")
Location: 4471 Route 9, Millbrook | Effective Date: March 1

1. GRANT OF FRANCHISE
Franchisor grants Franchisee the right to operate one Golden Griddle restaurant at the above location, using Franchisor's trademarks, recipes, and operating system, for an initial term of 10 years from the Effective Date.

2. ROYALTY AND MARKETING FEES
Franchisee shall pay Franchisor a continuing royalty fee of 6% of Gross Sales, plus a marketing fund contribution of 2% of Gross Sales, both payable monthly by the 10th of the following month. Total ongoing fees under this Agreement are therefore 8% of Gross Sales combined. Franchisee acknowledges reviewing a prior year's Franchise Disclosure Document that stated a 7% royalty rate for agreements executed that year; that document does not apply to this Agreement, which was executed this year under the updated terms reflected in this Section 2.

3. TERRITORY
Franchisor grants Franchisee an exclusive territory with a 3-mile radius from the location above, within which Franchisor will not license another Golden Griddle location during the term of this Agreement. Franchisee acknowledges that franchise agreements for certain other regions, including a separate franchisee's agreement covering a rural territory, use a 5-mile exclusivity radius instead, reflecting lower population density in that other region; that 5-mile figure does not apply to Franchisee's own territory here, which uses the 3-mile radius stated above and nowhere else.

4. INITIAL FEE
Franchisee paid a one-time initial franchise fee of $45,000 upon signing, which is non-refundable except as required by applicable franchise law in Franchisee's state.

5. OPERATING STANDARDS
Franchisee must operate in accordance with Franchisor's Operations Manual, as amended from time to time, including required hours of operation, approved suppliers, and quality standards, subject to periodic inspection by Franchisor's field representatives at reasonable intervals.

6. TERM AND RENEWAL
This Agreement has an initial term of 10 years, renewable for one additional 10-year term if Franchisee is in good standing, has met sales performance benchmarks in the Operations Manual, and pays a renewal fee equal to 20% of the then-current initial franchise fee at the time of renewal.

7. TERMINATION
Franchisor may terminate this Agreement for uncured material breach, including failure to pay royalties within 30 days of the due date, following written notice and a 15-day cure period. Franchisee may terminate for convenience with 180 days' written notice, subject to a post-termination non-compete of 2 years within the exclusive territory described in Section 3 above.

8. SAMPLE ROYALTY CALCULATION (FOR ILLUSTRATION ONLY)
For a month with Gross Sales of $85,000: royalty fee = 6% x $85,000 = $5,100. Marketing fund contribution = 2% x $85,000 = $1,700. Total fees due = $6,800 for that month, payable together by the 10th of the following month per Section 2 above.

9. GENERAL
This Agreement, together with the current Franchise Disclosure Document provided to Franchisee before signing, is the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes any prior year's disclosure document or discussion, including the 7% royalty figure referenced in Section 2.

10. INSURANCE
Franchisee must maintain general liability insurance of at least $1 million per occurrence and name Franchisor as an additional insured on the policy throughout the term of this Agreement, providing proof of coverage annually or upon request.

11. SIGNAGE AND BRANDING
Franchisee must use only Franchisor-approved signage, uniforms, and packaging, updated at Franchisee's own expense whenever Franchisor introduces a new approved design system across the brand.

SIGNATURES
For Golden Griddle Quick-Service Franchising LLC: Gideon Farley, VP Franchise Development
Franchisee: Marisol Vega

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Franchisee acknowledges having received and reviewed the current Franchise Disclosure Document at least 14 days before signing this Agreement, as required by applicable franchise disclosure law, separate from any prior year's version discussed above.

KESTREL AEROSPACE PARTS — SOFTWARE LICENSE COMPLIANCE AUDIT
Prepared by: IT Asset Management (Lead: Anouk Verstappen)
Date Issued: February 12
Scope: Annual review of installed software against purchased license counts, all business units

METHODOLOGY
Auditors used an automated software-discovery scan across all company-issued laptops and servers, cross-referenced against procurement records of purchased license counts for each title, for all software titles with more than 10 installations company-wide as of the scan date, consistent with the scope used in each of the past three annual audits.

FINDING: DESIGNSUITE PRO
The discovery scan found 45 active installations of DesignSuite Pro, a CAD design tool used primarily by the engineering team. Procurement records show only 40 licenses were purchased under the current agreement with the vendor. This represents a compliance gap of 5 unlicensed installations, a violation of the vendor's licensing terms that could expose the company to audit penalties if discovered by the vendor directly rather than caught internally first.

FINDING: PROJECTTRACK
The scan found 22 active installations of ProjectTrack, a project-management tool used by program management. Procurement records show 30 licenses were purchased. This is the opposite situation: 8 purchased licenses are not currently assigned to any active installation, representing potential cost savings if the license count were right-sized to actual usage, since being over-licensed is not itself a violation of any vendor term, unlike the DesignSuite Pro shortfall above.

ROOT CAUSE: DESIGNSUITE PRO GAP
Investigation found the 5 extra installations were set up for five contractors brought on for a short-term project in November, whose onboarding used a shared internal image that included DesignSuite Pro by default, without a corresponding license request being filed with IT Asset Management as required by the software provisioning policy in effect at the time.

REMEDIATION: DESIGNSUITE PRO
IT Asset Management purchased 5 additional DesignSuite Pro licenses on February 5, bringing the company into full compliance, at a cost of $2,400, 5 units at $480 per license, the vendor's standard per-seat annual rate. The provisioning policy was also updated so that any image including DesignSuite Pro now triggers an automatic license-request ticket, rather than relying on the requester to remember to file one separately.

DISCUSSION: PROJECTTRACK RIGHT-SIZING
IT Asset Management recommends reducing the ProjectTrack license count from 30 to 24 at the next renewal, 22 currently active plus a small buffer for near-term hires, which would reduce annual spend by approximately $1,800 assuming a per-license rate similar to the title's typical market pricing, without affecting any currently active user of the tool.

AUDIT FREQUENCY PROPOSAL
One IT Asset Management team member proposed moving from an annual license audit to a quarterly cadence, to catch compliance gaps like the DesignSuite Pro issue faster than an annual cycle allows. This was discussed and not adopted as a full quarterly audit cycle, given the overhead of running the full discovery-and-reconciliation process four times a year across all business units. Instead, the team adopted automated monthly usage reports for the top 10 software titles by installation count, which should surface a gap like this one within a month rather than waiting for the next annual audit, without the overhead of a full quarterly audit process running company-wide.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Maintain full compliance on DesignSuite Pro; confirm the 5 new licenses are correctly reflected in next year's renewal quote.
2. Right-size ProjectTrack to 24 licenses at next renewal.
3. Roll out automated monthly usage reports for the top 10 titles by March 1.

SIGN-OFF
Reviewed and accepted by Anouk Verstappen, IT Asset Management Lead, February 12. This report will be shared with Finance for visibility into the ProjectTrack renewal savings opportunity ahead of budget planning.

#ops-oncall channel — exported chat log, May 3

[14:02] Keiko S.: Paging, MES dashboard for Line 2 just went unresponsive, operators can't log completed units
[14:03] Bram V.: acking, looking now
[14:05] Bram V.: confirmed, Line 2's MES instance is not responding to health checks. Line 1 and Line 3 dashboards both look fine, they're on separate MES instances so this looks isolated to Line 2's box specifically
[14:06] Keiko S.: ok good, at least it's not all three lines. what's the impact on Line 2 physically, are they stopped?
[14:08] Bram V.: checking with the floor now
[14:10] Bram V.: floor says Line 2 is continuing to run, operators are logging completed units on paper as a fallback per the outage runbook, will need manual entry into MES once it's back up
[14:15] Anders F.: found it, connection pool on Line 2's MES database is exhausted, 100 of 100 connections in use, all held by a single long-running reporting query that's been executing for 47 minutes straight
[14:17] Anders F.: that reporting query is the new daily yield-summary report someone added last week, it's doing a full table scan on the shift-log table without an index, seems to run fine on smaller data volumes in staging but Line 2's production table is much bigger than staging's
[14:20] Keiko S.: can we just kill the query to free up connections?
[14:21] Anders F.: killing it now
[14:22] Anders F.: query killed, connections freed up, MES dashboard responding again
[14:25] Keiko S.: confirmed with the floor, dashboard is back, starting the manual paper-log backfill into MES now
[14:26] Bram V.: total downtime 14:02 to 14:22, so about 20 minutes of dashboard unavailability, though the line itself never actually stopped producing units, which is the main thing that matters for the shift's output numbers
[14:40] Keiko S.: backfill complete, all paper-logged units are now in MES correctly
[15:00] Anders F.: root cause: the new yield-summary report query lacks an index on the shift-log table's timestamp column, and the report isn't rate-limited or resource-isolated from the main MES connection pool at all
[15:05] Keiko S.: fix plan?
[15:06] Anders F.: two things: add the missing index today, and move reporting queries to a read replica instead of hitting the primary MES database directly, so a bad report query can't starve the production connection pool again
[15:10] Bram V.: agreed, let's prioritize the read-replica work this week given how directly it would prevent a repeat of today's incident
[15:30] Keiko S.: separate topic while we're all here, has anyone revisited the proposal to consolidate all three lines onto one shared MES instance? saw it mentioned in last month's infra review doc
[15:32] Bram V.: yeah, and today is actually a good argument against it. if all three lines shared one instance, this exact same runaway query would have taken down all three lines' dashboards instead of just Line 2's
[15:33] Anders F.: agreed, the isolation is exactly what limited today's blast radius, I'd push back hard on consolidating now
[15:35] Keiko S.: fair points, I'll note in the infra review thread that today's incident is a concrete reason to keep the lines on separate MES instances rather than consolidating them
[15:40] Bram V.: I'll write up the postmortem doc tonight, will include the connection-pool graph showing the exhaustion ramp so it's easy to see in the retro next week
[15:42] Anders F.: thanks, I'll add the index fix and read-replica ticket links to it once both are filed
[15:45] Keiko S.: appreciate the fast turnaround today everyone, good example of isolation working as intended even under a messy failure

ANCHORLINE SHIPPING — CONSTRUCTION SITE INCIDENT REPORT
Site: Port Calder Warehouse Expansion | Report No. CON-INC-0019
Incident Date: July 11 | Report Date: July 16
Prepared by: Site Safety (Lead: Theo Marsh)

INCIDENT SUMMARY
At 12:05 p.m. on July 11, a section of scaffolding on the east wall of the warehouse expansion partially collapsed. The area had been cleared for the midday lunch break at 12:00 p.m., 5 minutes before the collapse, per standard site schedule, and no workers were in the immediate area when the collapse occurred. No injuries were reported. The collapsed section covered approximately 30 feet of scaffolding at the second and third tiers, striking a stack of empty pallets below but no other equipment or materials.

RESPONSIBLE PARTY
The scaffolding was erected and maintained by subcontractor Ironclad Scaffolding Co. under its standard subcontract with Anchorline's general contractor. Investigation found the collapsed section's cross-bracing had been installed with only 2 of the required 4 bracing connections at that section, a deviation from Ironclad's own installation standard and the scaffolding manufacturer's specification.

UNRELATED EVENT: BRIGHT ELECTRIC
Separately, on July 9, an electrician employed by a different subcontractor, Bright Electric, received a minor shock from an unlabeled live wire during rough-in work on the second floor. That incident was investigated and closed separately as CON-INC-0018, with corrective action already completed, requiring all live circuits to be labeled and locked out before any adjacent rough-in work begins. It is unrelated to the scaffolding collapse and involves a different subcontractor and a different root cause entirely; it is mentioned here only because both incidents occurred at the same site within the same week and appeared together in this week's site safety summary.

INVESTIGATION FINDINGS
Ironclad's site foreman stated the missing bracing connections were an oversight during a rushed section handoff between two crews on July 10. No inspection sign-off had been completed for that specific section before crews moved to the next section, which should have caught the missing bracing under Ironclad's own quality process before it was ever left standing overnight.

DISCUSSION OF RESPONSE OPTIONS
General contractor leadership discussed terminating Ironclad's subcontract immediately given the severity of what could have been a serious injury or fatality had the collapse occurred during working hours. This was discussed and not adopted as an immediate termination; instead, Ironclad was required to submit a corrective action plan within 5 business days and undergo a full third-party structural inspection of all currently standing scaffolding on site before resuming any new scaffolding work, with continued work on already-inspected, unaffected sections permitted to continue in the meantime under close supervision.

CORRECTIVE ACTION PLAN STATUS
Ironclad submitted its corrective action plan on July 15, within the required window, committing to double sign-off on all bracing connections going forward and additional foreman training on handoff procedures between crews. The third-party inspection is scheduled for July 18; new scaffolding work is paused pending that inspection's results.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Complete the third-party inspection by July 18 before authorizing any new Ironclad scaffolding work.
2. Require double sign-off on all bracing connections for the remainder of this project, per Ironclad's own corrective action plan.
3. Site Safety to conduct unannounced spot checks on scaffolding bracing at least weekly for the remainder of the expansion project, given this finding.

SIGN-OFF
Approved by Theo Marsh, Site Safety Lead, and the General Contractor's Project Manager, July 16.

DISTRIBUTION
Copies of this report were sent to Anchorline Shipping's corporate safety office and to Ironclad Scaffolding Co.'s regional manager for acknowledgment and inclusion in the project's ongoing safety file, with a follow-up status update due after the July 18 inspection results are received.

RESELLER PARTNER AGREEMENT
Between Vantage Analytics LLC ("Vantage") and Pinnacle Business Solutions, Inc. ("Partner")
Effective Date: January 1

1. APPOINTMENT
Vantage appoints Partner as a non-exclusive authorized reseller of Vantage's dashboard analytics products to Partner's own customer base, effective on the date above.

2. COMMISSION STRUCTURE
An earlier draft of this Agreement, circulated November 10, proposed a flat 15% commission on all contract value regardless of year. That draft was not adopted. Under this Agreement, Gold-tier partners, see Section 3, earn 20% commission on first-year contract value and 10% commission on each subsequent renewal year for deals they source and close. Silver-tier partners earn 15% on first-year value and 7.5% on renewals.

3. PARTNER TIER AND QUOTA
Partner begins this Agreement at Gold tier. To maintain Gold tier, Partner must generate at least $50,000 in new booked contract value each calendar quarter. If Partner falls below $50,000 in new bookings in any quarter, Partner is downgraded to Silver tier for the following two quarters, after which Gold tier can be reinstated if the $50,000 quarterly threshold is met again for one full quarter at Silver-tier performance.

4. Q1 PERFORMANCE RECORD
Partner's Q1 new bookings totaled $38,000, below the $50,000 Gold-tier quota. Per Section 3, Partner was downgraded to Silver tier effective Q2, covering Q2 and Q3, the two quarters following the shortfall quarter.

5. Q2 PERFORMANCE RECORD
Partner's Q2 new bookings totaled $62,000, above the $50,000 threshold. However, per Section 3, the downgrade period following a shortfall quarter is fixed at two full quarters regardless of performance during those quarters; Partner remains at Silver tier for Q2 and Q3 despite the strong Q2 performance, with Gold tier eligible for reinstatement starting Q4 if Q3 also meets the threshold.

6. MARKETING SUPPORT
Vantage provides co-branded marketing materials and up to $5,000 per quarter in marketing development funds for Gold-tier partners, reduced to $2,000 per quarter for Silver-tier partners during any quarter at that tier.

7. TERM AND TERMINATION
This Agreement has an initial term of 2 years, renewing automatically for 1-year terms unless either party gives 60 days' notice of non-renewal. Either party may terminate for uncured material breach with 30 days' notice and a 15-day cure period.

8. EXCLUSIVITY
This is a non-exclusive arrangement; Partner may resell competing analytics products, and Vantage may appoint other resellers within Partner's same territory at its own discretion.

9. REPORTING
Partner must submit a quarterly bookings report to Vantage within 10 business days of quarter close, which forms the basis for the tier determinations described in Sections 3 through 5 above.

10. GENERAL
This Agreement supersedes the November 10 draft and any prior discussions regarding commission structure or partner tiers between the parties.

11. TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION
Partner's sales staff must complete Vantage's online product certification within 30 days of this Agreement's Effective Date and annually thereafter, as a condition of remaining eligible to earn commissions on any new deal, regardless of Partner's current tier.

12. LEAD REGISTRATION
Partner must register any prospective deal with Vantage's deal-registration system before beginning active sales discussions, to establish which party sourced the opportunity for commission purposes; deals not registered before a conflicting registration by another partner or Vantage's own direct sales team are not eligible for Partner's commission under Section 2.

13. DISPUTE RESOLUTION
Any dispute regarding tier status, commission calculation, or deal-registration priority under this Agreement will first be escalated to each party's designated partner-program manager for informal resolution before either party pursues any other remedy available under this Agreement or applicable law.

SIGNATURES
For Vantage Analytics LLC: Elliot Ferris, Director of Partner Programs
For Pinnacle Business Solutions, Inc.: Samir Kassab, Managing Partner

ALDERPOINT HEALTH — CLINICAL RESEARCH DATA INTEGRITY AUDIT
Study: ALP-204 (Phase II) | Site: Alderpoint Health Research Site 3
Prepared by: Clinical Quality Assurance (Lead: Tariq Idris)
Audit Date: August 19-21 | Report Date: August 28

SCOPE
This audit reviewed source-document-to-EDC, electronic data capture, data entry timeliness and accuracy for all case report forms (CRFs) completed at Site 3 between May 1 and July 31, per Good Clinical Practice requirements and the study's Data Management Plan, which requires CRF data entry within 72 hours of a study visit for every visit type across the protocol.

METHODOLOGY
Auditors compared source documents, visit notes and lab results, against EDC entry timestamps for a random sample of 40 CRFs out of 210 completed in the review period, checking both entry timeliness and data accuracy against source documentation.

MAJOR FINDING: LATE DATA ENTRY, WEEK 12 VISITS
Three CRFs, all for the Week 12 study visit across three different patients, were found with EDC entry timestamps more than 72 hours after the documented visit date, ranging from 96 to 140 hours late. Per the Data Management Plan, entry beyond the 72-hour window without a documented, pre-approved exception is classified as a major finding, since Week 12 data feeds directly into the study's primary efficacy endpoint analysis and late entry raises data-integrity concerns specific to that analysis. Investigation found the site's primary data-entry coordinator was on unplanned medical leave during that period, and CRFs were queued rather than reassigned to a backup entry person, which the site's own procedures require but which did not happen in this case.

MINOR FINDINGS: TRANSCRIPTION DISCREPANCIES
Separately, auditors found 12 instances across the 40-CRF sample of minor transcription discrepancies, such as a lab value entered as 4.5 when the source document showed 4.8, none of which affected any primary or secondary efficacy endpoint and all of which were within the study's pre-specified acceptable-deviation range for that data field. These are classified as minor findings under the Data Management Plan and do not require an individual corrective action plan, though they are logged for the site's ongoing quality trend tracking going forward.

DISCUSSION
The major finding, late entry on 3 Week 12 CRFs, is the only finding in this audit requiring formal corrective action under the study's quality procedures. The 12 minor transcription discrepancies, while more numerous, fall within the acceptable-deviation category and are handled through routine quality tracking rather than a corrective action plan.

DISCUSSION OF RESPONSE OPTIONS
The study sponsor's quality team discussed replacing Site 3's EDC system with a different vendor's platform, reasoning that a more modern interface might reduce data-entry delays going forward. This was discussed and not adopted; the audit found the delay was caused by a staffing gap during medical leave, not by any deficiency in the EDC platform itself, which performed correctly and simply reflected whenever data was actually entered into it. Replacing the platform would not have addressed the actual root cause and was judged disproportionate to this finding.

CORRECTIVE ACTION REQUIRED
1. Site 3 to submit a corrective action plan within 10 business days addressing backup-coverage procedures for data entry during staff absences.
2. Site 3's Week 12 data for the three affected patients to undergo an additional source-data verification pass by the study monitor before database lock.
3. All site data-entry staff to complete refresher training on the 72-hour entry requirement and backup-coverage procedure by September 15.

SIGN-OFF
Reviewed and accepted by Tariq Idris, Clinical Quality Assurance Lead, August 28. A follow-up audit of Site 3's corrective action plan implementation is scheduled for October, prior to the study's planned database lock in November.

MEADOWBROOK PUBLIC LIBRARY BOARD
Regular Meeting Minutes
Date: March 11 | Recorded by: Rosalind Kanu, Board Secretary

ATTENDANCE
Present: Chair Beatrice Adeyemi, Members Gideon Farley, Consuela Marques, Tariq Idris. Library Director: Wanjiru Kamau.

CALL TO ORDER
Chair Adeyemi called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

LATE FEES DISCUSSION
Director Kamau presented a proposal, based on research from peer library systems, to eliminate late fees for standard circulating materials, citing evidence that late fees disproportionately affect lower-income patrons and often cause people to avoid the library entirely rather than return items, reducing overall circulation over time. Two versions of the proposal were discussed. The first version would eliminate late fees entirely, including on the library's rental collection of new releases and mobile hotspots, which currently generates return-incentive value from fees given their high demand and limited copies. The second version would eliminate late fees for all standard circulating materials but retain fees specifically for the rental collection, to preserve return incentives for the small number of high-demand, limited-copy items where late fees currently do meaningful work encouraging prompt return. After discussion, Gideon Farley moved to adopt the second version, eliminating late fees for standard materials while retaining them for the rental collection. Consuela Marques seconded. The motion passed 4-0. The first version, eliminating all fees including on the rental collection, was not brought to a separate vote once the second version passed.

FINANCIAL IMPACT
Director Kamau presented the financial analysis: eliminating late fees on standard materials is estimated to reduce annual fee revenue by $18,000. However, staff currently spend an estimated equivalent of $12,000 per year in staff time processing fee payments, handling fee disputes, and processing fee waivers for hardship cases, time that would be freed up for other patron services once most late fees are eliminated. The net estimated annual cost of the change is therefore approximately $6,000, which the board considered acceptable given the goals described above.

BUDGET REVIEW
Treasurer functions were covered by Director Kamau in the absence of a dedicated board treasurer this cycle. Total library budget for the fiscal year is $1.2 million, funded primarily through the county allocation with a smaller portion from the Friends of the Library fundraising group. The $6,000 net cost of the late-fee change will be absorbed within the existing materials and programming budget without requiring a budget amendment, since it represents roughly one half of one percent of the total budget.

IMPLEMENTATION TIMELINE
Kamau proposed implementing the change effective May 1, allowing time to update the library's automated notice system and signage throughout all branches. The board did not object to this timeline.

EXISTING FEE BALANCES
Marques asked whether existing unpaid late fees already on patron accounts would be forgiven retroactively. Kamau confirmed yes, all existing late fees for standard materials, not rental-collection items, will be cleared from patron accounts as of the May 1 effective date, so patrons are not still blocked from borrowing due to old fees under the policy being eliminated.

PUBLIC COMMENT
Three community members spoke in favor of the change during public comment, citing personal experience with fees discouraging library use in the past. One member also asked whether the rental collection's continued fees might similarly discourage some patrons from borrowing new releases; Kamau acknowledged the tradeoff but noted the board judged the return-incentive value there to outweigh that concern given the limited copies available.

ADJOURNMENT
Meeting adjourned at 7:40 p.m. Next meeting: April 8, at which the board will review early results from the May 1 rollout if any preliminary data is available by then.

Minutes respectfully submitted by Rosalind Kanu, Board Secretary.

Between Cobalt Peak Software, Inc. ("Acquirer") and Fernglass Analytics, Inc. ("Target")
Date: September 8

This Letter of Intent ("LOI") sets out the parties' preliminary understanding regarding a possible acquisition of Target by Acquirer. EXCEPT FOR SECTIONS 4 (EXCLUSIVITY), 5 (CONFIDENTIALITY), AND 6 (GOVERNING LAW), THIS LOI IS NOT BINDING ON EITHER PARTY AND CREATES NO OBLIGATION TO CONSUMMATE A TRANSACTION.

1. PROPOSED TRANSACTION
Acquirer proposes to acquire 100% of Target's outstanding equity for an estimated purchase price in the range of $12 million to $15 million, subject to adjustment based on due diligence findings, final negotiated terms, and a definitive purchase agreement. This range reflects the parties' current, preliminary understanding only. An earlier verbal discussion between the CEOs in August referenced a possible $10 million price floor; that figure does not appear in this LOI and is not part of the range stated above, which the parties agreed supersedes any earlier verbal discussion between them.

2. STRUCTURE
The transaction is contemplated as a stock purchase, with Target's existing management team expected to continue in their roles post-closing, subject to definitive employment agreements to be negotiated separately from this LOI.

3. DUE DILIGENCE
Target will provide Acquirer reasonable access to its financial records, customer contracts, and technical infrastructure for a due diligence period of 60 days from the date of this LOI, to inform the final purchase price and terms of any definitive agreement.

4. EXCLUSIVITY (BINDING)
For 45 days from the date of this LOI, Target agrees not to solicit, encourage, or engage in discussions with any other party regarding a sale, merger, or similar transaction involving Target. If Target breaches this exclusivity provision, Target shall pay Acquirer a break-up fee of $500,000, which the parties agree is a reasonable estimate of Acquirer's costs and is Acquirer's exclusive remedy for a breach of this Section 4.

5. CONFIDENTIALITY (BINDING)
Both parties will keep the existence and terms of this LOI and any information exchanged during due diligence confidential, except as required by law or to their respective advisors under confidentiality obligations of their own.

6. GOVERNING LAW (BINDING)
This LOI, including its binding provisions, is governed by the laws of the state in which Acquirer is headquartered.

7. NO OBLIGATION TO PROCEED
Nothing in this LOI obligates either party to enter into a definitive agreement. Either party may terminate discussions at any time prior to signing a definitive purchase agreement, subject to the exclusivity and confidentiality obligations above continuing to apply for their stated durations even if discussions are terminated early.

8. NEXT STEPS
The parties intend to negotiate and execute a definitive stock purchase agreement within the 60-day due diligence period described in Section 3, though this timeline is itself non-binding and may be extended by mutual written agreement of both parties.

9. FEES AND EXPENSES
Each party bears its own legal, accounting, and advisory fees and expenses incurred in connection with this LOI and the proposed transaction, regardless of whether a definitive agreement is ultimately signed by either party.

10. NOTICES
All notices under this LOI, including any notice of breach of the binding provisions above, must be delivered in writing by email to each party's signatory below, with a copy to that party's outside counsel of record.

SIGNATURES
For Cobalt Peak Software, Inc.: Bram Vandermeer, VP Corporate Development
For Fernglass Analytics, Inc.: Keiko Sano, CEO

This LOI reflects the outcome of three weeks of preliminary discussions following the August verbal conversation between the CEOs. The $10 million figure discussed then was an early, informal anchor point before either side had reviewed Fernglass's actual financials in any detail.

SOLMERE ENERGY — CORPORATE FACILITIES ENERGY AUDIT
Facility: Solmere Energy Headquarters, 220,000 sq ft | Report Date: April 30
Prepared by: Facilities Sustainability (Lead: Ottilie Brandt)

BACKGROUND
As part of Solmere Energy's internal sustainability commitments, Facilities Sustainability conducts an annual energy audit of company-owned facilities, benchmarking each against an internal target energy use intensity, EUI, of 55 kBtu per square foot per year, a target set three years ago based on peer benchmarking for comparable office buildings in the region and reviewed annually for continued relevance.

HEADQUARTERS FINDINGS
The Headquarters building's trailing 12-month EUI is 68 kBtu per square foot per year, 24% above the 55 kBtu/sqft/year internal target. This represents a slight increase from last year's 66 kBtu/sqft/year, continuing a pattern of the building missing target for three consecutive years running.

HEADQUARTERS ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
The audit identifies the HVAC system, original to the building's 1998 construction, as the primary driver of excess energy use, operating at an estimated 35% below the efficiency of current-generation equipment. A secondary factor is the building management system, BMS, which lacks zone-level scheduling and currently runs full HVAC operation building-wide from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. regardless of actual occupancy in any given zone, including floors with significantly lower occupancy since the shift to hybrid work three years ago.

COMPARISON: RIVERSIDE DATA ANNEX
For comparison, the company's Riverside Data Annex, a smaller 40,000 sq ft facility housing IT infrastructure and a support team, achieved an EUI of 48 kBtu per square foot per year this year, under the 55 kBtu/sqft/year target. This facility underwent an HVAC and BMS upgrade two years ago, which the audit believes is the primary reason for its favorable performance relative to Headquarters; the two facilities are not directly comparable in function, but Riverside's post-upgrade performance is cited as an internal proof point for what a similar upgrade could achieve at Headquarters.

DISCUSSION OF RESPONSE OPTIONS
Facilities initially proposed a full HVAC system replacement at Headquarters, estimated at $2.1 million, projected to bring the building close to or under the 55 kBtu/sqft/year target. Given budget constraints this year and the multi-year timeline such a project would require, leadership decided not to fund the full replacement immediately. Instead, the company is funding a $180,000 building-management-system upgrade, adding zone-level occupancy sensing and scheduling, projected to reduce EUI by approximately 15% based on the Riverside Annex's experience with a similar BMS component, without yet replacing the HVAC hardware itself this year.

PROJECTED IMPACT OF BMS UPGRADE
A 15% reduction from the current 68 kBtu/sqft/year would bring Headquarters to approximately 58 kBtu/sqft/year, still 3 kBtu/sqft/year above the 55 target but a meaningful improvement, and one that could be measured within one year rather than the multi-year HVAC replacement timeline, before deciding whether the larger investment is still needed once the BMS upgrade's actual results are in hand.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Proceed with the $180,000 BMS upgrade at Headquarters, targeting completion by Q3.
2. Re-measure Headquarters EUI one year after BMS upgrade completion before deciding on the HVAC replacement question.
3. No facility-wide capital request for HVAC replacement this budget cycle, pending BMS upgrade results.

OTHER FACILITIES
Two smaller regional sales offices were also reviewed this year and both came in within 5% of their individual targets, requiring no corrective action; their detailed figures are omitted from this summary since neither showed a material finding worth reporting alongside Headquarters and Riverside above.

SIGN-OFF
Reviewed and accepted by Ottilie Brandt, Facilities Sustainability Lead, April 30. This report will be shared with the executive sustainability committee at its next quarterly meeting for awareness and budget planning purposes.

REDGATE COMPONENTS — WAREHOUSE DAMAGE INCIDENT REPORT
Facility: Central Distribution Warehouse | Report No. WH-DMG-0091
Incident Date: August 14 | Report Date: August 19
Prepared by: Warehouse Operations (Lead: Wanjiru Kamau)

INCIDENT SUMMARY
At 10:40 a.m. on August 14, forklift operator Colin Draper, while backing out of Aisle 7 to reposition for another pick, struck a storage rack, causing one pallet of finished marine hardware, bound for a customer shipment to Anchorline Shipping, to fall and sustain damage. No injuries occurred; Colin was the only person in the immediate area at the time and reported the incident to his supervisor immediately.

DAMAGE ASSESSMENT
The damaged pallet contained 340 units of marine cleats and fittings, of which 210 were found damaged beyond use upon inspection, valued at $32.38 per unit, totaling $6,800 in damaged inventory. The remaining 130 units on the pallet were undamaged and returned to stock after inspection confirmed their condition and structural integrity.

ROOT CAUSE
Aisle 7 has a known blind spot at its intersection with the main cross-aisle, due to tall storage racking on both sides limiting sightlines for reversing equipment. Warehouse policy WH-11 requires a spotter for any forklift reversing maneuver in aisles marked with congestion signage, but Aisle 7 was not marked with congestion signage at the time, since that signage criteria has historically been applied only to aisles with cross-traffic from multiple pick zones, which Aisle 7's layout did not technically meet despite its blind-spot geometry. No spotter was present for Colin's reversing maneuver, consistent with the aisle not requiring one under the signage-based policy as written at the time.

UNRELATED EVENT: ROOF LEAK DAMAGE
Separately, on August 22, a different pallet in Aisle 12 sustained $1,200 in water damage during a storm, due to a roof leak that Facilities has since patched. This is an unrelated incident with a different cause, weather and building maintenance rather than equipment operation, and is included in this month's damage summary total only because both incidents fall within the same monthly reporting period; it should not be conflated with the August 14 forklift incident described above in any way.

MONTHLY DAMAGE SUMMARY CONTEXT
Combined, this month's two incidents total $8,000 in damaged inventory, $6,800 from the August 14 forklift incident and $1,200 from the August 22 roof leak, against a monthly damage budget threshold of $10,000 that would trigger additional executive review if exceeded; this month's combined total remains under that threshold.

DISCUSSION OF RESPONSE OPTIONS
Warehouse Operations discussed requiring a spotter for every forklift reversing maneuver warehouse-wide, regardless of aisle signage, as the most conservative possible response available. This was discussed and not adopted; leadership determined this would slow warehouse throughput significantly across dozens of low-risk aisles with good sightlines, for a benefit concentrated in a small number of blind-spot aisles like Aisle 7. Instead, the congestion-signage criteria in WH-11 is being revised to include a new "limited sightline" category based on rack geometry, not just cross-traffic volume, which will bring Aisle 7 and similarly-configured aisles under the mandatory-spotter requirement going forward.

CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
1. Add congestion/limited-sightline signage to Aisle 7 and audit all other warehouse aisles for similar blind-spot geometry by September 1.
2. Update WH-11's signage criteria to include the new limited-sightline category described above.
3. Colin Draper to complete a reversing-maneuver refresher, standard practice after any rack-strike incident regardless of fault determination.

SIGN-OFF
Approved by Wanjiru Kamau, Warehouse Operations Lead, August 19. This report has been shared with Anchorline Shipping's account manager to explain the delay in fulfilling the affected shipment, along with a revised delivery estimate for the replacement units still needed to complete that order in full.
